regime: Trend-Up but Fading (Tech Lags, Gold and Crude Lose Their Stops)
summary: The tape split: the broad market held while tech faded and both metals and oil lost their trend lines. NQ opened under Tuesday's close, stretched all the way down to its minus 3 sigma band near 31,191, then reverted to close 31,406, down 0.30 percent on the day but green from its lows. ES held firmer and closed 7,850, up 0.26 percent, so the S&P stayed the steadier of the two. The real movers were the havens and oil: December gold fell 1.33 percent and closed below its ATR stop, and crude faded its 90.27 open to close 88.94, down 1.07 percent and back under the stop it flipped up on Tuesday, before ripping past 91 overnight. VIX ticked up to 15.58, still a calm sub-16 read.

risk.openRisk: Trend-long exposure in gold and crude is off, both closed below their stops.
risk.note: Throttle stays NORMAL with VIX at 15.58 and both index futures still above their stops. The caution is that the tape thinned and split: NQ's stop is now falling, and gold and crude both lost their trend lines, so systematic trend-long exposure there is flat until price reclaims those stops. Intraday ranges widened (MNQ one-sigma near 47 points versus 33 on Tuesday), so keep size standard and let the stop lines decide exposure. The shutdown keeps federal data on hold, so expect headline-driven moves, like tonight's crude spike, rather than scheduled catalysts.

psychology: Watch how fast a one-day signal can flip. On Tuesday both gold and crude flipped their ATR stops up and looked like fresh longs. One session later both closed back below those same lines. Anyone who married Tuesday's flip and pressed size gave the move back today. The fix is not a sharper forecast. Let the stop line make the call, and size each trade so one failed flip is a small planned loss. That way a day like today costs you a little and teaches you a lot.
